bullets.text: Missed calendar-year 96 CR goal with Q1 CR at 99.0 (March at 106.2); PL CR 98.7; CL CR 98.4; profit remains Core Value ahead of growth.
Prior accident year reserves developed unfavorably 4.6 pts on companywide CR, primarily vehicle repair costs; loss severity up nearly 10% YOY; frequency relatively flat.
Personal auto rates increased 4% in Q1 after rising over 13% in 2022; commercial rates rose 6% in 2022, while the company plans aggressive rate increases over 2023.
Companywide NPW grew 22% YOY; Personal Lines NPW rose 25%; Commercial Lines NPW increased 15%, but was basically flat excluding TNC business; Property NPW reached $629 million, up 17% YOY.
Companywide PIF +9% YOY; PL PIF +10%, supported by increased quotes, conversion, and renewal apps; Property PIF up 4% with new applications +12%.
Catastrophe losses added 1.8 points to companywide CR (versus 1.2 points in Q1 2022); the company was affected by 24 catastrophic weather events, primarily March storms, compared to 11 in Q1 2022.

Advertising spend rose 23% YOY, putting upward pressure on calendar-year expense ratio; planned policy acquisition investments across Agency and Direct channels are being evaluated to help meet calendar-year profit goals.
Debt-to-total capital declined to 27.5% from 28.7% at year-end 2022; investment portfolio returned 2.3% (fixed income 2.0%, equity 7.3%), shifted conservatively toward cash and Treasuries.

Restricting new Commercial Lines business in certain geographies and segments until rate increases take effect; continuing to evaluate underwriting, bill plan offerings, and operational discipline on expense management to meet profit targets.
Property rates raised ~3% in Q1 (~20% trailing four quarters); business concentrating growth away from coastal and hail-prone regions toward auto bundles and newer construction.
